provenance_note: The reference corpus was written by an independent agent without access to this tool's code (own settled-moment solver, ref.py); this run recomputes every check from the shipping build.
reference: Planar two-leg sling cases (symmetric at 10/30/44.9/45.1/59.9/60.1 deg, offset CG with hook above CG and with hook off the CG line, coordinate and leg-length geometry, dynamic factor and g scaling, overloads of sling/shackle/hook, missing WLL, zero-load and slack legs, flip-over and degenerate geometry, invalid inputs), symmetric four-leg cases with n = 2 and n = 4 effective legs plus four-leg refusals, and 30 seeded random two-leg geometries. Numbers are recomputed by ref.py: the rigid load with taut legs is turned about the hook until the CG is below it, and tensions are taken from moment balance about the opposite lifting point (cross-checked with a 2x2 force solve), not from Lami/Cramer as the tool describes.
reference_citations: Rigid-body statics: three-force concurrency, force and moment equilibrium of a load hung from two inextensible legs (ref.py)

HOIST Magazine, 'Sling geometry and forces', https://www.hoistmagazine.com/analysis/sling-geometry-and-forces/ (read 2026-09-16): 0-45 and 45-60 deg rating ranges; rigid four-leg load effectively two-leg; load tilts until horizontal components balance
Spec specs/07.md, acceptance criteria and 'Модель, правила и проверки'; specs/00-common.md 0.5 (insufficient data)
tolerance: Numbers: relative 1e-9 (absolute 1e-9 where the reference is 0; force residual |sum F|/W <= 1e-9 absolute). Every quantity is closed-form trigonometry and a 2x2 linear solve with no iteration, so any difference above floating-point rounding (~1e-13 here) is a model difference; 1e-9 is also the closure criterion the tool states. Angle limits (45/60 deg) are user inputs in every case and boundary cases sit 0.1 deg either side, so no rounding ambiguity. Categorical and boolean checks are exact.

not_benchmarked.Tilt display threshold: Exact 0.1 deg display threshold of the tilt warning (a tool design choice, no source); only tilt 0 and tilts of several degrees are checked.
not_benchmarked.Heuristic triggers: CG-above-attachment-points heuristic (SLG-H-001) and phi = 1 heuristic (SLG-F-001): no source fixes their trigger; random and headline cases keep the CG below the points.
not_benchmarked.Behaviour at the angle limits: Behaviour exactly at the 45/60 deg limits (inclusive vs exclusive) - no source text read that settles it.
not_benchmarked.Slack-leg hang geometry: Angles and geometry of the further-rotated single-leg hang in slack cases (tool states it does not compute them).
not_benchmarked.Standard clause values: EN 13414-1 / EN 818-4 / EN 1492-1 clause values and multi-leg rating factors; ISO 12480-1 wording (standards not read). Limits are supplied as inputs.
not_benchmarked.Outside the planar model: 3D rigging, four-leg asymmetric plans, sling stretch, PDF/sketch/drag UI, Python export.

coverage: Covers MVP: 2-leg planar tensions with CG offset and unequal geometry (analytic + random), symmetric 4-leg with stated effective-leg count, included vs from-vertical convention, utilisation against user WLL (sling/shackle/hook), dynamic factor, angle attention/maximum boundaries on both sides, slack and non-load-sharing legs, hook-not-above-CG warning, insufficient data, refusal of indeterminate (4-leg offset CG) and degenerate configurations, and the acceptance criteria on force residual and printed angle convention.

harness.note: tools.petrov.re safety harness (qa.mjs): manifest, catalog, 1280/390 px in seven languages, report PDFs, permalink, Python export self-test.

python_export.note: standard-library script reproduces every recorded output within 1e-9 relative.

independence.note: author's own harness against an independently written corpus; not an independent validation.
